questions.stem:
Monocyclic compounds P, Q, R and S are the major products formed in the reaction sequences given below.
3-Phenylpropanoic acid —(i) Br₂/Red phosphorus (ii) H₂O→ P
Benzaldehyde + acetaldehyde —aq. NaOH, 293 K→ Q
Phenylacetylene —(i) NaNH₂, allyl bromide (ii) Hg²⁺, H₃O⁺→ R
2-Methylindene —(i) O₃, Zn-H₂O (ii) CH₃MgBr (2 equiv.) (iii) H⁺, Δ→ S
The product having the highest number of unsaturated carbon atom(s) is
questions.solution: P (HVZ) is PhCH₂CHBrCOOH: 6 aromatic C + COOH = 7 unsaturated carbons. Q is the cross-aldol product of PhCHO and CH₃CHO (at most cinnamaldehyde, PhCH=CHCHO, 9). R: the acetylide is allylated to PhC≡CCH₂CH=CH₂, and Hg²⁺ hydration gives PhCOCH₂CH₂CH=CH₂: 6 + 1 + 2 = 9. S: ozonolysis opens the five-membered ring of 2-methylindene to o-(2-oxopropyl)benzaldehyde; two CH₃MgBr add to both carbonyls and acid/heat dehydrates both alcohols, giving o-CH₂=CH–C₆H₄–CH=C(CH₃)₂: 6 + 2 + 2 = 10. S has the most.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; matches the official key printed in the paper (D)

questions.stem: The correct reaction/reaction sequence that would produce a dicarboxylic acid as the major product is
questions.solution: (A) 2-Chloroethanol → 3-hydroxypropanenitrile → 3-hydroxypropanoic acid: only one COOH. (B) Bromine water oxidises only the CHO of glucose, giving gluconic acid (one COOH). (C) Alcoholic KOH dehydrohalogenates bromocyclohexane to cyclohexene, and hot acidic KMnO₄ cleaves the C=C to give adipic acid, HOOC(CH₂)₄COOH, a dicarboxylic acid. (D) Chromic acid oxidises the CH₂OH to COOH, giving a β-keto monocarboxylic acid (the ketone is untouched).

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; matches the official key printed in the paper (C)

questions.stem:
For the reaction sequence given below, the correct statement(s) is(are)
Tetralin —(i) KMnO₄, H⁺, Δ (ii) NH₃, Δ, −2H₂O→ X —(i) Strong heating (ii) Ethanolic KOH (iii) R-Br→ Y —NaOH→ Aromatic compound + Z

options.text: Both X and Y are oxygen containing compounds.
Y on heating with CHCl₃/KOH forms isocyanide.
Z is an aromatic primary amine.

questions.solution: Hot acidic KMnO₄ oxidises both benzylic positions of tetralin to give phthalic acid; with NH₃ and loss of 2 H₂O this gives phthalamide/phthalimide (X), and strong heating gives phthalimide. Ethanolic KOH forms potassium phthalimide, which is N-alkylated by R–Br to N-alkylphthalimide (Y) — the Gabriel synthesis. NaOH hydrolysis releases sodium phthalate (the aromatic compound) and the primary aliphatic amine R–NH₂ (Z). X and Y both contain oxygen (A true); Y has no N–H₂ group, so no carbylamine reaction (B false); Z is a primary amine and reacts with Hinsberg's reagent (C true) but it is aliphatic, not aromatic (D false).

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; matches the official key printed in the paper (A, C)

questions.stem:
For the reaction sequence given below, the correct statement(s) is(are)
Lactone —LiAlH₄→ P —CrO₃-H₂SO₄→ Q —NaOH and CaO, Δ→ R; P —H₂SO₄, 443 K→ S

options.text: Q gives effervescence with aq. NaHCO₃.

questions.solution: LiAlH₄ opens the δ-lactone to the diol HOCH₂CH₂CH(CH₂Ph)CH₂CH₂OH (P). The carbon bearing the benzyl group now carries two identical CH₂CH₂OH arms, so P is achiral and optically inactive (A false). Jones oxidation converts both primary alcohols to COOH, giving 3-benzylpentanedioic acid (Q), which liberates CO₂ with NaHCO₃ (C true). Soda-lime decarboxylates both acids to (CH₃)₂CHCH₂Ph, an alkane, not an alkyne (D false). Concentrated H₂SO₄ at 443 K dehydrates both alcohols to the diene CH₂=CH–CH(CH₂Ph)–CH=CH₂, which decolourises Baeyer's reagent (B true).

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; matches the official key printed in the paper (B, C)

questions.stem:
A linear octasaccharide (molar mass = 1024 g mol⁻¹) on complete hydrolysis produces three monosaccharides: ribose, 2-deoxyribose and glucose. The amount of 2-deoxyribose formed is 58.26 % (w/w) of the total amount of the monosaccharides produced in the hydrolyzed products. The number of ribose unit(s) present in one molecule of octasaccharide is ______.
Use: Molar mass (in g mol⁻¹): ribose = 150, 2-deoxyribose = 134, glucose = 180; Atomic mass (in amu): H = 1, O = 16
questions.solution: A linear octasaccharide has 7 glycosidic links, so hydrolysis adds 7 H₂O: total mass of monosaccharides = 1024 + 7 × 18 = 1150 g per mole. 2-Deoxyribose = 0.5826 × 1150 = 670 g = 670/134 = 5 units. The other 3 units weigh 1150 − 670 = 480 g; with a ribose and b glucose units, a + b = 3 and 150a + 180b = 480, giving a = 2, b = 1. So there are 2 ribose units.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; matches the official key printed in the paper (2)
